admission.justification: The named real-operation regression witnesses protect against false restore acceptance or destructive cancellation caused by a mismatched native merge or index-byte read.

applicability: Both-changed parked paths requiring native acquisition, without independent exact raw/fingerprint ownership; restoration diagnostic disclosure is separately limited to its bounded named-path recomputation.
conditions: A failed effective-configuration read or native merge leaves no computed expectation for a both-changed path requiring that merge; no fallback or alternative algorithm supplies acceptance.

Restoration fails while its native expectation is unavailable; cancellation may instead preserve unattributable state in durably written saved files before rolling back and restoring the parked candidate. The complete stash inventory and terminal-before-retirement boundary remain.
Restoration names at most the first ten failed paths inline, with readable merge rules and a remainder count; its full failed-name log is not an exhaustive inline native-reason channel.

The restoration refusal includes Git command/exit/reason only when reapply_merge_fault recomputation over failures[:10] invokes the lazy native merge and captures a fault. A native-dependent failure outside that sample does not imply that its reason appears in the refusal.

Cancellation carries the native fault captured by its ownership assessments into the saved-cancellation summary. This producer is separate from bounded restoration named-path recomputation and promises no identical reason for every failed path.

Fresh saves use durable atomic writes and record SHA-256 of the written payload; recovery of prior completed manifests reopens and verifies their named bytes. Fresh-save durability is not an independent reread of every artifact.
exclusions: Equal-content/base cases need no native acquisition.
An undefined driver name can conform when Git chooses the same built-in text merge for proof and reapply.
Exact raw stash holders and retained fingerprints remain separately scoped ownership evidence.

Exhaustive restoration-reason disclosure: when every named diagnostic path takes an equality/base/simple-content case, recomputation has no native fault even if a later failed path needed failed native acquisition.
Unreadable carried-head attributes do not disclose a merge rule; the full failed-path name log does not enlarge the bounded inline rule/reason population.

evidence: ReapplyMergeTests::test_a_merge_git_cannot_make_fails_its_path_and_no_other_merge_stands_in in mcp/tests/test_sync_reapply_merge.py, with an injected fault of `git merge-tree` and of the configuration read (both sub-cases fail on attempt 1, where the sync ended `synced` through a plain file merge: finding L163-RV-3, evidence-A2/tests-before-attempt1-git255.log and -git243.log); the texts in evidence-A2/refusal-texts-candidate.log; freeze 96c3e0ca + tree fe29dd94 (attempt 2); report role-launch/260928-MIK-L163-worker-A2.md

origin.handoffEntry: MIK-R162 failure clause (no merge of the proof's own)

statement: Where native merge or effective-configuration acquisition cannot establish a both-changed path, restoration fails without another construction; cancellation retains the actual fault, saves unattributable bytes before rollback, and never treats failed proof as ownership.
